title: Lighthouse: Consolidated Pool Signals & Burst Override Composer
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Operators managing dedicated GPU pools currently need to jump between multiple views (health timeline, burst templates, autoscale knobs, cost panes) to diagnose and remediate short-duration surges. Context switching increases time-to-action and makes it hard to perform quick overrides during incidents.

Goal: Design a single, compact composable surface — 'Lighthouse' — that surfaces the most relevant pool signals, quick diagnostics, and a safe, auditable burst override composer. It should be operable by SREs and platform engineers with minimal clicks, provide contextual decision support (suggested burst sizes, predicted cost delta), and integrate with rollouts and audit logs.

Scope:
- Top-level condensed health signal strip (latency p50/p95, queue depth, GPU utilization, mem pressure) with time anchors.
- Inline diagnostic expansion per signal (e.g., expand p95 to show contributing models/routes).
- Burst Override Composer: a guided flow to request temporary capacity, choose source pool or burst tokens, preview estimated cost and latency changes, and create a scoped audit log entry.
- Safe-guards: suggested guardrails (max burst %, cooldown), preview of rollback triggers, and a one-click 'revert' in the same surface.
- Integration: link to rollouts (canary AB) and to Reserve/Capacity view to surface reserved vs. burst capacity.
- Accessibility: keyboard-first interactions for critical controls, ARIA labels for all status chips.
- Performance: UI must render within 200ms for surface open and support streaming updates for the signal strip.

Non-goals: Full replacement of existing detailed dashboards; long-term capacity planning tools (placed in a separate workspace).
acceptance_criteria: Lighthouse surface prototypes available in Figma with desktop + narrow panel responsive variants
Prototype demonstrates 3 signal expansions and the full Burst Override Composer happy path
Design provides copy for each affordance and clear error/confirmation states
Edge cases documented: concurrent override attempts, insufficient quota, failed rollout rollbacks
Handoff artifacts: component spec, tokens, and interaction flows for engineering
notes: We should prioritize the safety modal and audit trail integration before exposing the free-form burst slider to non-admins.
